question: What universal maximum service life, in years, does the MUTCD assign to every traffic sign before mandatory replacement?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not assign any universal maximum service life, in years, to traffic signs. None of the provided evidence establishes a fixed replacement age for all signs; the MUTCD instead addresses sign condition through maintenance and retroreflectivity provisions rather than a mandatory age-based replacement schedule. The evidence supplied here (which concerns sign sizes, placement, and general purpose) is insufficient to support the premise of the question. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2H-1, which lists General Information sign and plaque sizes, not service life. [Image 2] (Figure 2A-2) illustrates heights and lateral locations of sign installations, with no service-life content. [Image 3] (Figure 2A-3) shows example locations of typical signs at intersections, with no service-life content. [Image 4] (Figure 2A-4) relates sign chapters/locations, not replacement intervals. [Images 5–8] are full-page views (table of contents, sign figures, and enhanced conspicuity examples) that contain no provision on sign service life. Citations: - Section 1A.01 Support §1 (p.1) - Table 2H-1 (p.460) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52)
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
